skill.name: domain-profiles
skill.description: Domain-specific profiles for creating educational resources across technology, history, science, arts, and general language topics. The profiles guide source selection, metadata collection, terminology handling, content structure, and review criteria.
skill.summary: Guide research and writing agents with domain-specific learning resource profiles.
skill.author: BitYoungjae

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, inline code formatting, or policy text that forbids dangerous patterns. No executable scripts, shell command sinks, unauthorized network behavior, or prompt-injection attempts were found in the reviewed files. The official Python documentation URL is used only as a citation example.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples resemble command execution to simple scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Label fenced examples as documentation snippets and prefer explicit language identifiers where practical.
Keep these examples in clearly marked review-policy sections and state that they are prohibited patterns.

remediation.issue: The technology profile contains an external documentation URL example.
remediation.suggestion: Use official documentation links only, and avoid placeholder API endpoints that could look like runtime calls.

content.value_statement: Generic research prompts often miss the structure and terminology required for each academic subject. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code domain profiles for source selection, writing structure, and review checks.
actual_capabilities: Maps technology, history, science, arts, and general topics to profile files.
Defines source priorities, search query patterns, and quality indicators for each domain.
Provides domain-specific metadata fields for learning resource planning.
Guides terminology, citation style, bilingual first-use wording, and content structure.
Supplies review criteria for research, writing, and reviewer agents.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not collect sources by itself.
It does not validate final documents with executable checks.
It covers five broad domains, not every academic specialty.
Some examples use Korean instructional text and may need localization.

use_cases.title: Plan a Domain-Specific Lesson
use_cases.description: Use the selected profile to define sources, metadata, terminology rules, and an outline before drafting.

use_cases.title: Guide Academic Research Collection
use_cases.description: Apply profile search patterns and quality indicators when gathering references for a learning project.

use_cases.title: Review Learning Materials
use_cases.description: Use the profile review criteria to check accuracy, structure, accessibility, and domain-specific requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Select the Profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the domain-profiles skill for this topic: {topic}. Identify the best profile and list the sections I should apply.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Research Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the matching domain profile for {topic}. Create a research plan with source types, query patterns, and quality checks.

prompt_templates.title: Structure a Learning Resource
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the selected domain profile to {topic}. Produce a lesson structure with terminology policy, special fields, and review criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Finished Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this learning draft against the relevant domain profile: {draft}. Report missing domain fields, terminology issues, and revision priorities.

output_examples.input: Topic: Python asynchronous programming for beginners.
output_examples.output: Selected profile: Technology. The plan prioritizes official documentation, runnable examples, environment details, and forbidden-pattern checks.

output_examples.input: Topic: Causes of World War I for high school students.
output_examples.output: Selected profile: History. The outline includes timeline context, primary-source notes, perspective balance, and historiography checks.
Selected profile: Arts. The resource should include visual examples, material specifications, practice exercises, and safety notes.

best_practices: Select the closest domain profile before research begins.
Apply search strategy and special fields before drafting content.
Use the review criteria before publishing or handing off the resource.
anti_patterns: Do not treat profile examples as source evidence.
Do not use the technology profile for every topic by default.
Do not look for general.md when the general domain maps to language.md.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It provides domain profiles that guide research, writing, terminology, and review for educational resources.

faq.question: Which domains are included?
faq.answer: It includes technology, history, science, arts, and general language profiles.

faq.question: Does it search the web automatically?
faq.answer: No. It gives source strategies and query patterns that another agent can use with available tools.

faq.question: Can it help with Korean learning materials?
faq.answer: Yes. Many profile examples include Korean educational wording and bilingual terminology guidance.

faq.question: Is it only for Claude?
faq.answer: No. The metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How should reviewers use it?
faq.answer: Reviewers can apply the profile criteria to check domain accuracy, structure, terminology, and quality requirements.
